extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a dataset for training reasoning models, containing 1.2 million examples across math (850K), code (250K), and science (100K) domains. The dataset was created through systematic experimentation with over 1,000 controlled experiments to optimize each step of the data generation pipeline, including question sourcing, filtering, teacher model selection, and answer generation.
extraction.creator: OpenThoughts-Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a multi-stage pipeline: (1) sourcing questions from existing datasets and newly generated datasets across math, code, and science domains, (2) mixing questions from top-performing sources, (3) filtering for high-quality questions using LLM-based methods, (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question (16x sampling), (5) generating answers using QwQ-32B as teacher model, and (6) final dataset composition with 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from multiple origins: (1) Non-synthetic: human-written questions from online forums (StackExchange, StackOverflow, CodeForces), contests (AIME, AMC, AOPS), and chatbot interactions; (2) Semi-synthetic: LLM-generated questions using existing data sources like CommonCrawl, FineWeb, and AutoMathText as seeds; (3) Fully synthetic: LLM-generated questions with minimal seed material (e.g., CodeAlpaca, CamelChemistry). Specific sources include OpenMath-2-Math for math, CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning for code, and StackExchange Physics and Organic Chemistry PDFs for science.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were filtered using LLM-based methods including difficulty-based filtering (asking GPT-4o-mini to rate question difficulty on a 1-10 scale) and response length filtering (annotating questions with LLMs and keeping questions with longest responses). For code, difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini was used. For math and science, response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini was applied.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing pipeline included: (1) Question sourcing from 27 code sources, 21 math sources, and 14 science sources; (2) Mixing strategy selecting top 1-2 high-quality sources rather than optimizing for diversity; (3) Question filtering using LLM-based methods (difficulty scoring, response length); (4) Deduplication using Indel similarity metric with exact match deduplication for math and science, no deduplication for code; (5) Sampling 16 answers per question from teacher model; (6) No answer filtering was applied as experiments showed filtering did not improve performance. Decontamination was performed against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram matching (N=13).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers and reasoning traces were generated using QwQ-32B as the teacher model. For each question, 16 independent responses were sampled from the teacher model. The teacher model generates long chains of thought (thinking tokens) during inference, which guide the model toward the correct answer. Responses include reasoning traces enclosed in <think> and </think> tags followed by the final answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Multiple answer filtering strategies were tested including majority consensus, GPT verification, FastText classification, and length-based selection. However, experiments showed that no filtering strategy outperformed using all generated answers without filtering. The study found that models with better benchmark performance are not necessarily better teachers - QwQ-32B was a stronger teacher than DeepSeek-R1 despite scoring lower on target reasoning benchmarks.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (teacher model for answer generation), GPT-4o-mini (for question generation, filtering, and verification tasks), GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano (for response length filtering), DeepSeek-R1 (used in earlier pipeline experiments), gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (for PDF text extraction)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is part of the OpenThoughts project with multiple generations of releases. OpenThoughts3-1.2M is the fourth generation following BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, and OpenThoughts2-1M. All datasets and models are available on openthoughts.ai.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work notes that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning inadvertently degrades pre-existing safety alignment of base models. OpenThinker3-7B achieved the highest harmfulness score (55.5) on Harmbench among tested models and was trained without any explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data. The findings underscore the challenge of balancing safety and utility in reasoning models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) The dataset focuses on SFT data curation and does not explore reinforcement learning datasets; (2) Staged SFT or curriculum learning approaches were not investigated; (3) Pipeline strategies were selected to maximize overall average benchmark performance rather than optimizing for each domain individually; (4) The study did not fully explore how data scaling behaves as student model performance approaches teacher performance; (5) Distilled reasoning models still show generalization deficits, exhibiting strong performance fluctuations on simple task variations despite improved average performance; (6) Some benchmarks show saturation at the largest scale (AMC23, MATH500) while others do not respond to scale (HLE).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of reasoning models. OpenThinker3-7B, trained on this dataset, achieves state-of-the-art results among open-data 7B models: 53% on AIME 2025, 51% on LiveCodeBench 06/24-01/25, and 54% on GPQA Diamond. The dataset is intended for training models with reasoning capabilities across math, code, and science domains. Usage guidelines emphasize that the dataset was optimized for average performance across domains and may benefit from domain-specific optimization for specialized applications.
